summary: A civic engagement API allowing citizen registration, report submission (with photos), and admin/municipality management of users, reports, roles, and comments. Includes authentication flows (login/logout/current user) and role-based access control for sensitive operations.

Documented responses: 200, 401

Returns 200 on success or 401 if not authenticated

authentication_notes: /auth/login is the primary entry point for authentication, returning session tokens or credentials.
/auth/current retrieves the currently logged-in user's details.
All operations tagged with 'Authentication' require prior login unless specified otherwise.
Admin-only operations require elevated privileges beyond basic authentication.
Operations marked auth_required need an authenticated session during test setup.
dependencies: POST /auth/login is a prerequisite for all authenticated operations.
POST /users/register-citizen creates citizens who can then POST to /reports/upload.
POST /users/register-user and related admin endpoints depend on successful login.
GET /reports/report/{id} depends on the existence of a report created via POST /reports/upload.
PATCH /reports/report/{id}/status, GET /reports/search-reports, PATCH /reports/report/{id}/assign, etc., all depend on the existence of a report and proper authentication.
POST /auth/login -> DELETE /auth/logout: Logout requires an active session established by login.
POST /auth/login -> GET /auth/current: Getting the current user requires an active session.
POST /users/register-citizen -> POST /reports/upload: Citizens must be registered before they can upload reports.
POST /users/register-user -> PATCH /users/edit-user: Editing a user requires the user to exist.
POST /reports/upload -> GET /reports/report/{id}: Retrieving a report requires the report to have been created.
POST /users/admin/create-municipality-user -> GET /reports/tos-users: Technical office staff users must be created before they can be retrieved.
POST /users/admin/create-municipality-user -> GET /reports/maintainer-users: Maintainer users must be created before they can be retrieved.
POST /users/admin/create-municipality-user -> GET /reports/assigned-to-techOfficer: Technical officers must be created and assigned reports before they can view their assignments.
POST /users/admin/create-municipality-user -> GET /reports/assigned-to-maintainer: Maintainers must be created and assigned reports before they can view their assignments.

risks: Ambiguity in role-based access control: Some endpoints specify 'admin only' while others say 'admin or municipality', which may lead to inconsistent permission enforcement.
Lack of explicit error handling details for common scenarios like duplicate usernames or invalid roles.
No clear indication of rate limiting or throttling policies for high-frequency operations like report uploads or comment additions.
Potential security risk if the 'password' field in request bodies is not hashed before storage, as indicated by the schema format.
